ifc_find.description: Find elements in the open IFC, filters combined: class (IfcWall …; every product when left out), name (contains), storey (exact name), where { "Pset_WallCommon.IsExternal": true }, or ids (GlobalIds). limit (50); detail: true adds psets, quantities, material. Answers elements [{ id, class, name, storey }].

ifc_open.description: Open an IFC file (path) to edit in place with IfcOpenShell: nothing is added to the FreeCAD document, and GlobalIds and all that is untouched stay as they are. One file at a time. Answers schema, storeys (elevation in the file's unit), classes (counts). The ifc_ tools exist only when FreeCAD has IfcOpenShell.

ifc_remove.description: Remove elements from the open IFC by GlobalId (ids, from ifc_find), with their openings and relationships. In memory until ifc_save; outside undo.

ifc_save.description: Write the open IFC with its edits: path (default <name>_edited.ifc in the output folder), or overwrite: true to write over the file it came from.

import_file.description: Bring a file into the current document (path; relative: the session's folder), by its extension. STEP, IGES, BREP: one body with the file's whole shape (split: true a body per solid); colours, part names and assembly structure are not read. STL, OBJ, 3MF, PLY, OFF, AMF and glTF/GLB, Collada, VRML 2, 3DS (every mesh node flattened into one, mm, Z up; units and up override what the format says; read says what was taken): a mesh (Mesh::Feature) unless solid: true asks for a body of its triangles (up to 200000; slow past a few tens of thousands). DXF: wires, arcs, circles, splines by layer (Agent Link's reader; a drawing with blocks, text or dimensions through FreeCAD's) and SVG as Draft geometry — many objects come back counted, the first few listed. JT where this FreeCAD has its reader. PNG, JPG, BMP: an image plane width mm wide on XY, to trace over. PDF, DWG, IFC need the FreeCAD window; FBX: export it as glTF; .FCStd: doc_open (doc_merge to bring its objects in). name: the label. Reply: format, count, objects (name, label, type, volume or mesh), health.

insp_export.description: Write an inspection out to the session's folder: <name>.csv with a row a point (x, y, z, distance_mm, status ok | over | under | out_of_reach) and <name>.json with insp_read's numbers. name: the files' base name (the inspection's label by default). Reply: files { csv { path, rows }, json { path } }, summary. The document is not changed.

insp_faces.description: An inspection split by the nominal body's faces: each face ("Body.Face4") with its points, mean offset (+ the actual sits outside there), min, max, rms and, with a tolerance, outOfTolerance and verdict — the faces that are off first; failing lists them. A face off evenly is displaced; one with min and max far apart is out of form. body: which body when the nominals hold several or none; reach mm (the search radius): how near a face a point must be to count for it; limit (30). Changes nothing.

insp_list.description: The inspections in the document, a line each: inspection, actual, nominals, points, rms, inTolerancePercent, verdict, outOfReachPercent. Changes nothing.

insp_read.description: One inspection's numbers (the one there is when inspection is left out): points, measured, outOfReach, min, max, mean, rms, stdDev, p95abs, histogram, tolerance, inTolerancePercent, over, under, verdict, worst spots (worst: how many, 10). Distances in mm, + outside the nominal. Changes nothing.

insp_run.description: Inspect with FreeCAD's own Inspection feature (left in the document): actual — a mesh, points or a body — or file (a scan: stl, obj, ply, off, 3mf, amf, asc, pcd, xyz) against nominals [bodies, meshes, points]. Nothing is aligned: put the actual where the nominal is first (object_align). search_radius mm (1; FreeCAD's own default is 0.05): a point further than that from every nominal reads out of reach, so it must reach past the tolerance. tolerance ±t or [low, high] mm gives the verdict. Distances are signed: + outside a solid nominal (material added), − inside. A mesh or scan is measured at its vertices; a body is meshed first (deflection 0.1 mm, points every spacing mm, default 1% of its size, at most cap 60000) and that hidden mesh measured (how says so). thickness is stored but FreeCAD 1.1 does not use it. Cost grows with points × nominal faces: a free-form body against a big scan takes minutes — raise spacing first. Reply: points, measured, outOfReach, min, max, mean, rms, stdDev, inTolerancePercent, verdict (pass only when all are in tolerance and none out of reach), worst [{ at, distance }], health. An estimate over a minute: the first call answers with the time and runs nothing, the same call again runs it.

insp_update.description: Change an inspection and measure again: search_radius, thickness, tolerance (±t or [low, high]; null clears), nominals — at least one; inspection may be left out when there is one. Checked before anything is set (a tolerance past the search radius is refused). Reply: as insp_run.

job_start.description: Run a call as a job: tool and its arguments. If it ends within 60 s, the answer is the tool's own. Else a job id (call-N) for job_status. wait: false gives the id at once. A client drops a call after about 80 s. So the server does this for any call past about 60 s. Not for job_ and app_ tools. No estimate refuses a call.

job_status.description: Read the state of a job. job: its id (call-N, or job-… for a heavy read). Answer: running (seconds so far), or done with the tool's answer or error. wait: seconds (up to 30) to wait first. No job: all jobs (kept for an hour). The server answers at once, also while FreeCAD is busy. Changes nothing.

link_edit.description: Change links: action replace { link, to } (point it at another object) | unlink { link, name } (a plain shape copy in its place, same placement; what used the link now uses the copy) | import { links } / import_all (objects linked from another document copied into this one). object_group { action: "list" } names the links.

link_make.description: A link (App::Link) to an object: it shows the object again without copying it and follows every change. to: the object (or "Box.Face3" for one element); at, axis + angle: the link's placement, which stands in for the original's own, not added to it; count: an array of that many elements, all starting at the same place, each its own object to place with object_set (reply: elements). kind: group makes an App::LinkGroup of objects. Reply: link, name, to, placement.

live_run.description: Replay a live window script (scripts/live, its README's format) and check every step's answers. Reset the test document first, every time: live_run { script: "reset" } closes what earlier runs left, rebuilds the WindowTest document and brings it to the front, and every other script is written to start from exactly that; run without it, a script acts on whatever document is in front and its checks fail for reasons that are not the tools'. script: a name (reset, agentlink, or another found in the installed add-ons' scripts/live folders; a wrong name is refused with the names there are) or a .json file's path. steps: only these (names or numbers from 0; all by default) — a later step run alone acts on whatever document is in front, with what the steps before it would have made missing. Each step's calls go to batch (rollback: false, stopOnError: false), or one by one when the step is direct; $names are filled in from vars { name: value } and from earlier answers (a $name the script declares, kept from the latest answer that has that key: $next); a step that needs one not known yet is skipped and says which. Two-role steps (role: student, parallel) are skipped: they need two agents (ROLES.md). Every expect is checked (equals, contains, atLeast, atMost, exists, noneContain with ignoreLinesWith; paths with dots, [*] any item, [-1] the last). A call with allow: [codes] may be refused with one of them without failing its step (allowedRefusals; reset closes documents that may not be open). A gui_input that opens a dialog does not end the replay: inside the dialog's loop, the step's calls after it and the next steps' calls run one at a time only while the dialog is still open (so the step that answers it runs); once it closes the replay returns, the dialog's loop ends, and the rest runs after it; a step answered busy is run again once after a short wait; anything left open at the end is closed (gui_unstick) and said in leftOpen. budget: seconds the replay may hold the window (90 by default, at most 600): no call starts past it, and the answer names the steps not run (notRun) — live_run { steps: [...] } runs them, so a long script is split across calls. A nested event loop still holding the window past the budget is closed, then the call is answered with what ran so far and FreeCAD is started again by the watchdog. The answer is always live_run's own summary. Reply: total { passed, failed, skipped, run } and steps, each with result pass, fail or skipped, a failing check's call, path, wanted and got, refused calls, the step's shot (a window picture, in the window) and look (what it should show), and the totals. stopOnFail: true stops at the first failing step. It changes the document as the script does.

material_clear.description: Forget what bodies are made of (bodies; every body with a material when left out). measure_mass then asks for a material again (a printed part is taken as PLA and says so); strength studies assume PLA and say so. FreeCAD's own ShapeMaterial on the object is left as it was. Reply: cleared, materials (what is still recorded).

material_get.description: One material's figures by id (a filament key, a library card's UUID or exact name, custom:<name>): density g/cm³, E (Young's modulus) MPa, nu (Poisson's ratio), yield and uts MPa, k W/(m·K) where the card has them, source, and missing (which of density, E, nu, yield the card lacks — fea needs E and yield, mass needs density). Library and filament figures are typical — a part that must not fail needs the supplier's. Changes nothing.

material_list.description: Find materials: words (every word must be in the id, name, category, tags or description) and category (part of one: "Printing filament", "Metal/Steel", "Thermoplast" …; the reply's categories lists them). The printing filaments (pla, petg, abs, asa, pa6-cf, tpu-95a) come first, then FreeCAD's material library (its cards with a density or stiffness; appearance-only, fluid and pattern cards left out), then this document's custom ones. Reply: found, materials [{ id, name, category, density g/cm³, E and yield MPa where the card has them }] (limit 20), more. A library card's id is its UUID; its exact name works wherever an id is asked. Changes nothing.

material_set.description: Say what bodies are made of: id from material_list (or a library card's exact name), or custom { name, density g/cm³ (required), youngsMPa, yieldMPa, utsMPa, poisson, conductivity W/(m·K), softensC, source } for the supplier's figures (kept as custom:<name>). Kept with the document by the body's label (measure_mass, fea_* and drawings read it there); a library card also goes on the object's ShapeMaterial, which FreeCAD's own Material panel shows (shapeMaterial says per body). An installed add-on that owns materials keeps those it knows (printing filaments), marked from. bodies: the one body when left out. Reply: material, mass_g (volume × density, solid through), missing (E / yield the card lacks). Trap: object_rename does not carry it to the new label. The short ids of measure_mass also work (steel, stainless, aluminium, brass …): the tool sets a FreeCAD library card for one, or Agent Link's stock figures; mapped tells which.

measure.description: Measure one thing or between two. a alone: a face's area (radius, diameter, axis when round; normal when flat), an edge's length (radius for a circle), a body's volume, area and box. a and b: the least distance (mm) with its two points (from, to), the angle in degrees between flat faces (their outward normals: 180 for opposite faces of a plate) or straight edges (0–90), or a line and a face's plane; gap between parallel faces' planes; centers between round ones' centres. References: "Face12" with body, "Box.Face12", a body's name (the whole shape) or a point [x,y,z]. Changes nothing; measure_keep keeps one in the document.

measure_keep.description: Keep a measurement in the document as one of FreeCAD's Measure objects (it follows the model and shows in the tree and the window). kind distance (two of: vertex, edge, flat or cylindrical face) | angle (two straight edges or flat faces) | length (one or more edges, summed) | area (one or more faces, summed) | radius (one circular edge, not a cylinder's face) | position (one vertex) | diameter (FreeCAD 1.1 has none: refused, use radius). of: the elements, ["Body.Face3", …] (a bare "Face3" when there is one body) — elements only, no points or whole objects. Trap: it is tied to face and edge numbers, which change after modelling steps; a measurement that then fails shows in health. Reply: measure (its label), value, unit. measure reads the same without keeping it.

measure_mass.description: Volume mm³, area, mass g, centre of mass and inertia (g·mm² about the centre of mass, document axes; principal moments and axes for one solid) of a body taken as solid through: FreeCAD's own shape mass is only the volume, so the density comes from material (pla, petg, abs, asa, pa6-cf, tpu-95a, nylon, pc, pom, acrylic, hdpe, steel, stainless, aluminium, aluminum, brass, copper, titanium, cast-iron, oak, pine, plywood, or a material_list id or name) or density g/cm³, else the material material_set recorded (a printed part with none is taken as PLA and says so). With neither given and an add-on that owns mass installed, its answer (as printed, inserts included) comes instead, marked from. Reply: density, densityFrom, volume, mass, centerOfMass, inertia. Changes nothing.

menu_list.description: The window's menu bar as the person sees it in the active workbench: items [{ path: [titles], command (its name for cmd_run), enabled: false when greyed, checked for toggles }]; menu: one top menu only (all of it; without it, the first limit 400 items). Menus change with the workbench. Window only. Changes nothing.

menu_run.description: Press a menu item by its path of titles (["View", "Standard views", "Fit all"]; as menu_list gives them, case and a trailing … aside). A greyed item is refused (it would do nothing), a submenu too, and what cmd_run refuses (modal dialogs, macros, quit). Reply: pressed, command, checked (a toggle's state after). Acts on the selection and the document in front, as cmd_run. Window only.

meshobj_boolean.description: A boolean of two closed meshes (meshobj_info: solid true): a, b, op union | intersection | difference (a minus b); a new mesh, a and b kept. Dense scans as they are: only the triangles the other mesh crosses are cut (built for scans of 100,000 triangles and more; time not measured, and a change cannot run as a job). Reply: how (which engine made it), solid, volume.

meshobj_boundary.description: A mesh's open edges as wires (Reverse Engineering's mesh boundary): loops, openEdges, boundaries [{ edges, length, closed, centre, area }] longest first (20); keep (default) makes them a wire compound to fill, sweep or fit. A closed mesh answers loops 0.

meshobj_curvature.description: A mesh's curvature: flatPercent (points under flat, 0.001 1/mm), tightestRadius and medianRadius mm, meanCurvature { min, max }. view_render { map: "curvature" } colours it. Changes nothing; on a dense mesh background: true runs it as a job.

meshobj_decimate.description: Fewer triangles: reduction (share to remove, 0.5) or facets (how many to keep); tolerance (0.1) caps the error one collapse may add, so it can stop short of the count (the reply's note says so: raise tolerance). Reply: reduced "n → m triangles", the mesh's reading, before.

meshobj_edit.description: Edit a mesh on a copy, as ScanRuler's Mesh Tools do: action begin { mesh } (a copy made, the original hidden; every meshobj tool given the original's name then changes the copy) | use (the copy put in place of the original) | discard (the copy dropped) | state (default: what is being edited).

meshobj_export.description: Write a document mesh to a file, the format by path's extension: stl (binary), ast, obj, ply, off, 3mf, amf, smf, wrl, x3d, iv, nas … (default <label>.stl in the out folder), where it stands, in mm. Reply: file, format, bytes, facets. Changes nothing; background: true runs a big one as a job.

meshobj_from_shape.description: Mesh a body (MeshPart) into a new mesh object: method standard (deflection mm off the surface, 0.05; angle deg, 15) | mefisto (maxLength mm: even triangles, but it can leave faces with small holes open: the reply warns) | netgen (fineness verycoarse … veryfine; unavailable where FreeCAD lacks it). A flat-sided body meshes to two triangles a face (a box: 12); a small deflection on a large curved body makes hundreds of thousands (reply: heavy). Reply: mesh, points, facets, solid, components, area, volume, box.

meshobj_info.description: A mesh's size and the Mesh workbench's evaluation: points, facets, solid (closed), components, area, volume, box; evaluation { nonManifolds, selfIntersections, flippedNormals, corruptedFacets, … }, problems, verdict clean or next. Changes nothing. The self-intersection test is slow on a dense mesh (not measured): background: true runs it as a job.

meshobj_merge.description: Put meshes into one mesh object where they stand (not fused: components stay apart; meshobj_boolean union fuses): meshes [names]; remove: true drops the originals. Reply: components, facets.

meshobj_offset.description: Move a mesh's surface along its point normals by distance mm (negative: inward); triangles the move turns over are collapsed, so a distance beyond the tightest inside radius damages the mesh: meshobj_info after. In place; copy: true makes a new mesh. Reply: offset, the mesh's reading.

meshobj_primitive.description: A mesh primitive (the Mesh workbench's regular solids): kind box (size [x,y,z], a corner at at) | sphere (radius, centred) | cylinder | cone (radius at the base, radius2 at the top, height; base centre at at, up +z) | torus (radius, radius2 the tube; centred, axis z); segments round (48). Reply: mesh, facets, solid, volume, box.

meshobj_project.description: Project a wire, sketch or body's edges onto a mesh along direction [x,y,z] (default down, [0,0,-1]); kept as wires on its surface. Reply: projection, wires, length.

meshobj_refine.description: More triangles: rounds 1 … 3, each putting a point in the middle of every triangle (about three times as many; refused past 2,000,000); optimize: true swaps edges to even their shapes. The surface does not change. Reply: refined "n → m triangles".

meshobj_repair.description: Repair a mesh as Evaluate & Repair does: fix any of normals, duplicates, nonmanifolds, selfintersections, degenerate, folds, indices, pointsonedges (default: those), holes (loops up to maxHoleEdges, 50, filled flat), islands (pieces of minFacets, 10, or fewer triangles dropped). Each step is kept only if it leaves no more open or overloaded edges (undone says which). Reply: did, fixed, problems (left), edges { open, overloaded }, before. In place; copy: true leaves the original. Evaluates twice: slow on a dense mesh, and a change cannot run as a job.

meshobj_sections.description: Cross-sections of a mesh as wires: normal (default z), count evenly spaced (5) or at [distances from the origin along normal], up to 500; tolerance mm joins cut ends (0.01). Reply: slices [{ at, loops, length }], sections (the wire compound; export writes DXF, part_face makes a face).

meshobj_segments.description: Find a mesh's flat regions: kind planar (deviation mm off a fitted plane, 0.01; about the noise on a scan) | curvature (both curvatures within tolerance 1/mm of 0); minFacets (20). Reply: segments (count), largest [{ facets, area, center, normal }] up to top (12); keep: true makes those meshes, each in a colour of its own in the window (as FreeCAD's Mesh_Segmentation colours its segments). On a scan: where to put a sketch. Slow on a dense mesh (every region is walked; not measured).

meshobj_smooth.description: Smooth a mesh: method taubin (default; shrinks far less than laplace, but a coarse mesh still loses volume; lambda 0.6307, mu 0.0424) | laplace (lambda; shrinks), iterations (3). Reply: volumeChange mm³ on a closed mesh, warning past 2%.

meshobj_split.description: Split a mesh into its separate pieces, a mesh object each, largest first (minFacets leaves out smaller ones; over 100 pieces is refused: raise minFacets). The original is hidden, not removed. Reply: pieces, facets.

meshobj_transform.description: Scale (a factor or [x,y,z]), rotate { axis, angle degrees }, move [x,y,z], mirror "x" | "y" | "z" a mesh's points, in that order, about the document's origin and axes. A mirror keeps the triangles facing out. In place; copy: true makes a new mesh.

meshobj_trim.description: Cut a mesh with a plane: at [x,y,z] on it, normal (the side it points to is removed); close: true caps the cut flat (loops up to maxHoleEdges, 1000); preview: true answers wouldRemove / wouldCut / wouldKeep and changes nothing. Refused when nothing would be left. Reply: removed (triangles wholly on that side), cut (triangles the plane crossed, each kept in part), solid, warning when the cap did not close it.

meshobj_unwrap.description: Lay a surface flat as a cutting pattern (sheet, fabric, leather): of a body's face "Body.Face3" or an open mesh in one piece. A plane, cylinder or cone face rolls out exactly; other faces and meshes go through FreeCAD's flatmesh (up to 50,000 triangles, run apart with a 5 minute limit; a closed mesh is refused). Reply: area3d, areaFlat, stretch { mean, max % }, outlines, size, pattern (the wire object; make: false keeps none); path .svg or .dxf writes it. tolerance mm tessellates a face (0.1).

note_add.description: Pin a note to the part for the person — a question or a remark (text): at [x,y,z] mm, or on body + faces ("Face6", or shape_query's filters; pinned at the first face's centre and found again when faces renumber). It shows as a numbered pin in the window and in Agent Link's Notes tab; the person answers it there. Kept in the document (saved with doc_save). Reply: note { id, text, at, body, face, by: agent }, note_count.

note_answer.description: Answer a note (the person's question or request): id (from note_list), text. The answer shows under the note in the window; a second answer replaces the first. note_done ticks it off once dealt with.

note_delete.description: Take a note out of the document for good: id — the person's or the agent's (note_done only ticks it off; delete the person's only when they ask). Reply: deleted, left.

note_done.description: Tick a note off: id (done: false opens it again). It stays in the document; note_delete removes it.

note_list.description: The notes pinned to the parts — the person's and the agent's — each with id, text, by, at, face, answer and done. waiting lists the ids of the person's notes with no answer yet (answer them: note_answer, then note_done); followed says which notes moved to a renumbered face. open: true leaves out the done ones. Read it at the start of a session and after the person has worked in the window.

object_align.description: Place an object by point pairs (what Std Alignment does by clicking): pairs [[from: a point on it now, to: where that point should be] …] in mm, document coordinates. One or two pairs move it only; three or more (not in a line) turn it too, the least-squares rigid fit — no scaling. Reply: rms and worst miss in mm (near 0 when the pairs agree), placement. Changes Placement only.

object_appearance.description: Colour objects: color "#rrggbb" or [r,g,b] 0–1 (or random: true), transparency 0 (solid) – 100, faces { "Face3": "#ff0000" } a colour per face (the rest keep the object's colour; face numbers change after a modelling step: shape_query again). Shown at once in the window; headless they are kept on the object (AgentLinkColor …) and exports read them. Reply: set [{ object, color, transparency, faces, shown }].

object_delete.description: Delete objects (objects: names or labels). Refused, nothing deleted, while another object uses one — FreeCAD itself deletes without asking and leaves the users broken, which force: true allows. Recomputes and lists any error. A PartDesign Body goes with its own features and Origin, and a boolean's result with the helpers made for it alone (alongWith names them); the inputs it hid are shown again and given their names back (shownAgain, renamed). Reply: deleted, errors, health. A container that only holds the object is not a user (a Body, an App::Part, a group): an unused sketch or the tip feature of a Body deletes without force, and the Body's tip moves back.

object_duplicate.description: Copy objects in the document (Std Duplicate): each copy is independent but still built from the same inputs (a copied Pad uses the original's sketch); dependencies: true copies what each is built from too; simple: true copies the shape alone as a plain Part::Feature (no history, placement baked in). name: the copy's label ("<label> copy" by default). Reply: duplicated [{ from, copy }].

object_freeze.description: Freeze objects (objects; frozen: false thaws) so recomputes leave their shapes as they are (Std Toggle freeze) — window only: FreeCAD 1.1 has no headless call for it, and the frozen state is not saved with the file. skipRecompute: true | false switches the whole document's recomputes off or on (works headless; recompute { force: true } still runs). Reply: frozen / unfrozen, not (those that did not take), skipRecompute. After thawing: recompute { force: true }.

object_get.description: One object's properties: value (mm, degrees; placements as { at, axis, angle }; links by label; a shape as its stats; lists cut at 50), type, readOnly (FreeCAD computes it: object_set refuses it), hidden (not shown in FreeCAD's property editor), choices for an enumeration. filter: a word in the property's name or group ("Placement", "Base"), or a list of exact names — use it, a feature has dozens. Changes nothing. Several words go in one filter with | between them ("Length|Width"): a property that has one of them matches.

object_group.description: Organise the document: action add | remove (objects into or out of group — made if new for add; kind folder (App::DocumentObjectGroup, placement-less) | part (App::Part: its Placement moves everything in it)) — an object sits in one group, so add takes it out of the one before; dissolve (the group goes, its objects stay); link (count App::Link copies of object, the first at, each step [dx,dy,dz] further — light copies that follow the original; at is the link's whole placement, not an offset from the original's); list (groups, parts and links with what they hold). visible: false hides a group's objects. Reply: group, type, holds.

object_list.description: Every object in the document: name (internal, fixed for life, unique), label (what the person sees and may rename), type, visible, parents (what uses it) and its shape (volume mm³, area, faces, solids, size for a solid; faces and edges else) or mesh; error: true marks a failed one (recompute gives the reason). type: part of the type to keep ("Part::", "Sketch"). Tools take either name or label; the name wins when both match. Changes nothing.

object_rename.description: Give an object a new label; its internal name never changes (FreeCAD fixes it at creation), and both keep working as references. A label another object has is refused (FreeCAD would alter it to stay unique unless its duplicate-labels preference is on). Expressions that use the label follow it. Trap: setups, specs and waivers keep the old label. Reply: name, from, to.

object_set.description: Set properties of an object: values { Length: 20, Placement: { at, axis, angle } (or FreeCAD's Base, Axis, Angle, Rotation; what is left out is kept), Refine: true, Base: "Box" (a link, by name or label; null clears), Mode: "…" } — each converted to its type: numbers are mm and degrees, or a string with a unit ("1 in", "30 deg") for lengths, angles and other quantities (not plain floats); whole numbers for integers and percents; enumerations checked against their choices; vectors [x,y,z]. Read-only properties, links to faces or edges and property names it does not have are refused (object_get lists names, types, choices). Recomputes the object and what is built from it; refused with nothing kept when that fails. Reply: set { from, to }, unchanged, health. Trap: a plain shape (Part::Feature from a boolean or import) has no sizes, only Placement; Label is set with object_rename. For one property, property and value also work: { property: "Length", value: 20 }.

outputs_clean.description: Clear the output folder of what Agent Link made there and no longer needs (only files it recorded making): shots past the last 50 and 3 days, solver and job runs past 14 days, FreeCAD backups past 7; exports only listed. To the Trash. Dry run unless dry_run: false; kinds, older_than_days narrow it. Runs on its own daily.

param_bind.description: Bind a property or a named, driving sketch constraint to an expression: target "Pad.Length" | "Sketch.width" (the constraint's name, not its number), expression "width" (a parameter by its name), "Params.width", "<Sheet>.<alias>", "Dims.size" (a variable set's, by its label or name) or "width / 2 + 1"; null unbinds (the value stays). One that does not evaluate or breaks a feature is refused, nothing kept. A bound value is then changed by param_set, sheet_set or varset_set, not edited directly. Reply: expression as kept, value, bodies.

param_list.description: The parameters: name, value, unit, what they are set to, and which properties use them; varsets: each variable set's variables (name, value, unit, ref, usedBy). Changes nothing.

param_remove.description: Remove a parameter no property uses (param_list shows usedBy; unbind each with param_bind expression: null first).

param_set.description: Set a named parameter in the Params spreadsheet (made when first needed): name (a letter, then letters, digits, _; not a cell address, a unit such as m, mm, s, N, or e / pi), value (a number with unit mm | deg | "", default mm; or an expression over others, "width / 2"), note. Everything bound to it recomputes; a value that does not evaluate or breaks a feature is refused with FreeCAD's error and nothing kept. Reply: value, unit, ref (Params.<name>), usedBy, bodies.

part_attach.description: Attach a primitive, wire or datum (not a plain modelling result) so it follows its support: to "Body.Face6", an edge, a vertex or a whole object; mode, a FreeCAD MapMode, by default FlatFace (flat face) | NormalToEdge (edge) | Translate (vertex) | ObjectXY (object); also Concentric, FrenetNB … (modes needing two references are not reachable). offset [x, y, z] and rotate degrees in the support's frame. Trap: a later boolean on the support renumbers its faces.

part_boolean.description: fuse, cut or common base with tools (solid bodies by name; base is the one kept, and must be named when more than one body is shown). common with several tools keeps what base shares with any of them. Done on the shapes, not as a Part::Cut feature: the result keeps base's label (name: a new one) as a plain shape with coplanar faces merged; the tools are removed (keep: true hides them; a hidden body is still a body to other tools). A PartDesign Body base gives a new Body on the result and the old one is hidden. Trap: faces and edges are renumbered; shape_query again. Refused, with the tools kept, when nothing would change (apart, or inside for fuse), common has no overlap, a tool is not a sound solid (invalid, open, inside out), or OCC drops a tool or makes an invalid result. Heavy with many faces (meshes made solids): past an estimated minute the first call answers with the time and runs nothing, the same call again runs it, and the window is frozen meanwhile. Reply: body, volume, box, sound (problems when not), op, volumeChange, removed or kept, hidden + hiddenNote (object_delete of the result shows the inputs again).

part_chamfer.description: Bevel edges of a solid body by size mm (the same on both faces). Edges are picked, numbered and refused as part_fillet's (edges refs from 1, "all", or query); reply as part_fillet.

part_compound.description: Group bodies into one compound (kept apart, not fused; it follows its parts): bodies [names] — or explode: the name of a body of several solids, each copied out as a body (the original hidden).

part_container.description: An App::Part container holding objects, moved together by its placement (Std Part): objects [names], at, axis + angle. Not a solid: booleans take the bodies inside it.

part_datum.description: A datum: kind point | line | plane | csys, at [x,y,z], normal (plane, line) or axis + angle; or attached by one reference (to "Box.Face6", an edge, a vertex), the placement then its offset. mode: a FreeCAD MapMode, by default by what to is (FlatFace, NormalToEdge, Translate; a line along a straight edge or a circle's axis; a point at a vertex or centre); a line on a face needs mode. Refused when it cannot attach.

part_defeature.description: Take features off a solid by their faces (Part defeaturing): faces ["Face12", …] numbered from 1 — every face of a hole, boss or fillet together; the faces around grow over the gap. Renumbers faces; refused when OCC cannot close it. For simplifying imported bodies before FEA or CAM.

part_extract.description: Copy elements out as a plain body of their own (Part's element copy and shape builder): refs ["Box.Face3", "Box.Edge2", whole objects], numbered from 1; build copy (as they are) | wire (edges joined) | face (closed edge loops filled) | shell (faces sewn at tolerance mm, 0.01) | solid (a closed shell made a solid; refused with a gap). Reply: shape, counts, valid.

part_extrude.description: Extrude a profile into a solid: length mm along its normal (a face's outward one; a flat outline's plane normal, +z in XY; negative goes the other way), or direction [x,y,z] (its own length, or length given); symmetric: half each way. op new (default without into) | fuse (default with into) | cut | common with into: a boss or a pocket in one call, refused when it misses into. solid: false gives a surface from an open profile. Done on the shape, not as a Part::Extrusion feature (no taper). A sketch used as profile is hidden; into's faces are renumbered. Reply: body, volume, area, faces, box, sound; with into also op, volumeChange. A surface (solid: false) answers as one instead: body, surface: true, faces, area, box, valid, openEdges (edges on its border) and closed — no volume, sound or solids, and it is not among session_state's bodies.

part_face.description: A flat face from closed wires or sketches in one plane: from [object names], the outline and any holes inside it (found by nesting).

part_fillet.description: Round edges of a solid body by radius mm. edges: ["Edge3", "Face6" (all its edges) …], numbered from 1 as shape_query lists them, or "all"; and/or query { type, axis, radius, near, inside, of: "Face6" … } as shape_query takes for edges. Done on the shape, not as a Part::Fillet feature: the body becomes a plain shape. Traps: every modelling step renumbers edges, so query again rather than reuse numbers; fillet last. Refused, nothing changed, when OCC fails or leaves a broken shape (a radius larger than a face beside the edge allows). Reply: body, volume, box, sound, edges (how many), volumeChange.

part_fix.description: Repair a shape: op reverse (flip an inside-out solid) | solid (closed shells or faces made solids) | sew (faces joined within tolerance mm, 0.01) | fix (ShapeFix at tolerance, 0.001). Reply: valid, closed, solids, notes.

part_from_mesh.description: A mesh made a solid, every triangle a face: mesh (an object) or file (STL, OBJ …); tolerance sews it, refine (default) merges flat triangles. For a closed, modest mesh: over maxFacets (60000) refused (meshobj_decimate first); thousands of faces already make it and every later boolean slow, the window frozen meanwhile. Of several pieces only the largest becomes the solid (note says so). refine about doubles the time; an estimate over a minute: the first call answers with the time and runs nothing, the same call again runs it.

part_import_curves.description: Import a curve network (the edges of a STEP, IGES or BREP; faces left out) as one object, for surface_fill or surface_sections: path (relative: in the session's folder).

part_join.description: Join walled objects (Part join features; inputs hidden): kind connect { objects } fuses walls keeping the insides; embed { base, tool } sets tool into base; cutout { base, tool } cuts base to fit tool's wall. Pipes and tanks. Reply: valid, solids, volume.

part_loft.description: A solid (solid: false: a surface) through two or more profiles in order: each a sketch, wire, face, { points, closed, smooth } (smooth: a B-spline through them), { points_file, key } or { circle }; or all from profiles_file (many sections read from a file, not sent in the call). All closed or all open. They are lined up first (same way round, seams nearest: aligned says what changed). ruled: true is straight between profiles, each made a polygon of samples points, so it always pairs up. Smooth (default): when OCC refuses or the loft bulges over 15% beyond the profiles it tries again itself (matching B-splines, maxDegree 3 then 2; maxDegree 1–8, default 5), then span by span with the bulging spans ruled (segments: false: off); route says what was done, a refusal names the spans. closed: back to the first profile. Refused, nothing added, when invalid, open or inside out. Heavy: time grows about as the cube of its faces (91 profiles of 36 points ruled 10 s; of 80 points over 2 min); past an estimated minute the first call answers with the estimate and runs nothing, the same call again runs it; a loft kept late says unchecked (run body_check). Reply: body, volume, box, sound, aligned, route, maxDegree, strays (how far it lies from the given points); a surface (solid: false) answers surface: true, faces, area, box, valid, openEdges and closed in place of volume and sound. op / into as part_extrude. More: guide_read { topic: "model" }.

part_offset.description: Grow (+) or shrink (-) a solid by distance mm all round (OCC's 3D offset, skin mode); join arc (rounded corners, default) or intersection (sharp). The body becomes a plain shape and its faces are renumbered. Refused, nothing changed, when OCC fails or no solid is left: shrunk past half the thinnest part or past a concave fillet's radius. Reply: body, volume, box, sound, distance.

part_offset2d.description: Offset a flat wire, sketch or face in its plane (Part::Offset2D; a closed wire goes through its face, as a plain shape): distance mm (+ out, − in), join arc | tangent | intersection, fill: true for the band between the two, intersection: true to offset several wires as one. Refused when the loop vanishes or is not flat. Kerf and clearance outlines, gasket bands.

part_primitive.description: Add a FreeCAD Part primitive as a body (mm, degrees). kind: box { size [x,y,z] }: a corner at at. cylinder { radius, height }, cone { radius (base), radius2 (top); either may be 0 }, prism { sides, radius (centre to corner), height }, tube { radius, radius2 (bore), height }: base centred at at, axis +z or along direction. sphere { radius }, torus { radius (ring), radius2 (tube) }: centred at at. wedge { wedge: { xmin, ymin, zmin, x2min, z2min, xmax, ymax, zmax, x2max, z2max } }: front face at ymin, rear face (x2, z2) at ymax. rotate { axis, angle } turns it about at. Parametric until a boolean, fillet or other part_ step bakes it to a plain shape: till then object_set changes Length / Width / Height (box x, y, z), Radius, Radius1 / Radius2 (cone base / top; torus ring / tube), Polygon / Circumradius, Xmin … Z2max, OuterRadius / InnerRadius. Reply: body, volume, area, faces, solids, box, sound, type, placement.

part_project.description: Project a wire's, sketch's or body's edges onto one face: shape (a name), onto "Body.Face6", direction [x, y, z] from the shape towards the face (left out: along the face's normals). Lettering wrapped onto a curved face, an outline traced onto a surface. Reply: edges, length, missed (wires that did not land).

part_refine.description: Merge a body's coplanar and co-cylindrical faces left by booleans (refine); a PartDesign Body gets its tip's Refine turned on and stays parametric. fix: true first repairs it (ShapeFix at tolerance mm, 0.001) and makes a closed shell a solid. Renumbers faces. Reply: faces { before, after }, done, sound.

part_revolve.description: Revolve a profile about an axis: axis [x,y,z] (default +z) through at [x,y,z] (default the origin), angle degrees (default 360; within -360 … 360, not 0). The profile must lie to one side of the axis (touching it is fine). solid: false gives a surface. profile, op / into and the reply as part_extrude (a surface's too: surface, faces, area, openEdges).

part_ruled.description: A ruled surface (parametric) of straight lines between two curves: a and b each an edge or wire by name, or one edge of a body as "Box.Edge3". reversed: true if it twists. A surface, not a solid (surface_thicken).

part_section.description: Section curves where a body meets another body (with: a parametric Part::Section; parametric: false for a plain shape) or a plane { normal, at }; face: true also fills the closed loops into a face. Refused when they do not meet. Reply: section, edges, length_mm, closedLoops, area_mm2. Cut-lines, outlines at a height.

part_slices.description: Cross-sections of a body: normal [x, y, z] (default z), count (1–500, evenly through it) or at [distances along the normal from the origin]; each slice's wires, length and material area (inner loops are holes), kept as one compound; range is the body's reach along the normal. Layer outlines, laser-cut stacks.

part_split.description: Split bodies (Part's BOPTools, parametric; inputs hidden, not removed): mode slice (bodies [one], tools [objects by name that cut right through it: a part_wire plane, a face copied out by part_extract, bodies]) | fragments (bodies: every piece where they overlap, kept apart) | xor (bodies: what is in an odd number of them); explode: true makes each piece a body. Reply: object, pieces, solids [{ volume, center }]; note when a slice cut nothing.

part_sweep.description: Sweep one closed profile (a face gives its outer outline) along a path: a wire or sketch, an edge "Box.Edge3", a helix from part_wire, or { points } (open by default). frenet: true keeps the profile from twisting along a helix; corners at sharp turns: right (default), round or none (FreeCAD's Transition Right corner, Round corner, Transformed). solid: false gives a surface, and then the profile may be open. Trap: the profile must already sit at the path's start, across it; it is not moved there. profile, op / into and the reply as part_extrude (a surface's too: surface: true, faces, area, box, valid, openEdges, closed — not a solid's sound and problems).

part_thickness.description: Shell one solid: open the faces named (open ["Face6"], numbered from 1, and/or query { normal: "+z", sort: "-z", limit: 1 }) and leave walls of thickness mm (above 0.002), inward by default (inward: false grows outward). join intersection (sharp, default) or arc. A body of several solids is refused (part_compound { explode } first). Traps: concave fillets smaller than the wall break an inward shell, so shell first and fillet after; faces are renumbered. Reply: body, volume, box, sound, thickness, inward, opened, volumeChange.

part_transform.description: Move or copy a solid body. move { by [dx,dy,dz] } and rotate { axis, angle degrees, about [x,y,z] (default: its box centre) } change its Placement in place (a primitive stays parametric); copy: true makes a new body instead. mirror { normal, about (box centre) } and scale { factor or [fx,fy,fz], about (origin) } make a new body and keep the original (mirror fuse: true joins both into the original). linear { count, step [dx,dy,dz] } and polar { count, axis, about (origin), angle (360 shares out evenly, less runs end to end) } array the body into itself, count with the original, fused (fuse: false keeps the copies apart in one body, quicker for many). Trap: all but move and rotate bake a plain shape and renumber faces and edges; shape_query again. Reply: body, volume, box, sound, op, and placement, from or count.

part_wire.description: A wire, curve or flat face as FreeCAD's own parametric object: kind line (from, to) | circle (radius) | arc (radius, start, end: 0–360° counter-clockwise) | ellipse (major, minor: full sizes) | polygon (regular: sides, radius to corners) | polyline (points, the corners in place, closed) | helix (pitch, height, radius, taper, leftHanded) | spiral (growth per turn, turns, radius) | plane (length, width) | bspline (points it passes through; closed: a smooth periodic loop; fit.maxDistance is how far it lies from them). at and normal place it: its centre (a plane's corner, a helix's base) at at, its z along normal. polyline and bspline take points_file (a .json list of [x,y,z] or a .csv of x,y,z rows in the session's folder; key picks one list) instead of points, so long lists are not sent in the call. Profiles and paths for extrude, sweep, loft; a plane cuts in part_split.

pd_binder.description: Bring another body's faces (or all of it) into this body as a shape binder (a SubShapeBinder), to sketch on or project from: from (body or feature), faces [{ at, normal } …] on it (none: the whole shape), frozen: true keeps it as it is now. Reply: binder, faces, next.

pd_body_new.description: Make an empty PartDesign body: the container a parametric part's features go in, with its own XY/XZ/YZ planes and x/y/z axes. Answers body: its label (name, made unique) to pass on. Next: sketch_new on one of its planes.

pd_boolean.description: A boolean inside a body with other PartDesign bodies: op fuse (default) | cut | common, with [body names]. The tool bodies move inside the boolean, stay editable and are followed; a fuse or cut that changes nothing is refused.

pd_chamfer.description: Bevel edges of the body: edges as pd_fillet; size mm (default 1); size2 for two distances or angle deg for distance and angle (one of them). On an inside corner it adds material, on an outside one it removes it: only a chamfer that changes nothing is refused. Reply: feature, volume mm³, volumeChange, faces, solids, box, health. A failure is refused with FreeCAD's error; nothing is kept.

pd_clone.description: A new PartDesign body on another object's shape (PartDesign Clone): from (a body, a Part solid, anything with a shape), at [x,y,z] and axis, angle to place it, name. Its first feature (BaseFeature) follows the original; pd_ features go on top. Reply: body, from, volume.

pd_datum.description: A datum: kind line (at, direction; along z by default), point (at) or lcs (a coordinate system: at, rotate { axis, angle }) placed from the body's origin; or on: { near: [x,y,z] } a round edge — its axis (line) or centre (point), attached so it follows the model. A line serves by name as an axis or direction. Reply: datum, at, direction.

pd_datum_plane.description: A datum plane in the body, on XY | XZ | YZ | a flat face query, offset mm along its normal, rotate { axis [x,y,z] (its own), angle deg }, name: for sketches off the body's planes (sketch_new { plane: its name }). Reply: plane, origin, normal.

pd_draft.description: Taper faces for moulding: faces [{ at, normal }] (or shape_query's references or filters), angle deg (1.5), neutral plane the faces pivot on (XY default, a datum plane, or a face; they must meet it), pull direction x|y|z (z) or a datum line, reversed. Reply: feature, volume mm³, volumeChange, faces, solids, box, health. A failure is refused with FreeCAD's error; nothing is kept.

pd_fillet.description: Round edges of the body: edges [{ near: [x,y,z] } the edge nearest a point | { face: { at, normal } } every edge of a face | { all: true }, kind: line|circle to filter], or what shape_query answers ("Edge3", "Body.Edge3", a list, its items) or its filters ({ type: circle, radius: 3 } every such edge; with near, the nearest); radius mm (default 1). References are good until the next change: query again after one. Smooth (tangent) edges are skipped. An inside corner gains material, an outside one loses it: both are right. Reply adds on (the edges). Reply: feature, volume mm³, volumeChange, faces, solids, box, health. A failure is refused with FreeCAD's error; nothing is kept.

pd_gear.description: An involute gear (kind gear: teeth, module, pressureAngle 20, shift, internal with rim mm of wall) or a roller-chain sprocket (kind sprocket: teeth, pitch 9.525 for #35 / 12.7 for #40, roller diameter) as a padded PartDesign feature on the body's XY plane: thickness, bore mm, at. Beside a solid already in the body it is a second solid. Answers the pitch and outside diameters.

pd_groove.description: Cut by revolving a closed sketch about an axis (inputs as pd_revolution). A groove that cuts nothing is refused. Reply: feature, volume mm³, volumeChange, faces, solids, box, health. A failure is refused with FreeCAD's error; nothing is kept.

pd_helix.description: Sweep a closed sketch's profile in a helix about an axis (default the sketch's V_Axis; H_Axis, x | y | z, a datum line, a line's id): two of pitch (mm per turn), height (mm), turns; taper (degrees) or growth (mm per turn, with height and turns: a spiral), leftHanded, reversed; subtractive: true cuts it (a thread, a groove). Keep the profile off the axis and under the pitch; many turns are slow. Reply adds helix.

pd_hole.description: Holes at the centre of every circle of a sketch (FreeCAD 1.1: at its points too; not construction geometry) on the face they enter, drilled against its normal: diameter mm, or thread "M5" (ISO coarse; "M8x1" fine) — threaded (default true: tap-drill size, cosmetic unless modelThread) or a clearance hole (threaded: false, fit close|normal|loose); depth mm | "through"; drillPoint flat|angled; cut counterbore|countersink|counterdrill with cutDiameter, cutDepth, countersinkAngle (a thread size gives standard ones). Reply adds holes, diameter, thread, cut. Reply: feature, volume mm³, volumeChange, faces, solids, box, health. A failure is refused with FreeCAD's error; nothing is kept.

pd_linear_pattern.description: Repeat features in a line: direction x|y|z (x) or a datum line, occurrences (2 or more, the original counted), spacing mm between copies or length mm first to last, reversed; features: "all" repeats the whole body. A grid: pd_multitransform. Reply: feature, volume mm³, volumeChange, faces, solids, box, health. A failure is refused with FreeCAD's error; nothing is kept.

pd_loft.description: Loft through closed sketches: profile (the first), sections [the rest, in order, each on its own plane], ruled, closed; subtractive: true cuts it. Sketches should have the same edge count and matching start corners, or it twists. Reply: feature, volume mm³, volumeChange, faces, solids, box, health. A failure is refused with FreeCAD's error; nothing is kept.

pd_mirrored.description: Mirror features (by name) across a plane: XY | XZ | YZ (default), a datum plane, or a face query; features: "all" mirrors the whole body (FreeCAD 1.1's TransformMode "Whole shape", else every pad and pocket up to the tip). A copy that misses the body makes a second solid (health says so). Reply: feature, volume mm³, volumeChange, faces, solids, box, health. A failure is refused with FreeCAD's error; nothing is kept.

pd_move_feature.description: Move a PartDesign feature (with its sketch, re-attached to the same origin plane) to another body: feature, to. It goes after that body's tip. Refused, with nothing moved, when it or what is left behind then fails (a pocket needs a solid to cut). Reply: moved, from, to, tip.

pd_multitransform.description: Repeat features through a chain of steps, each on what the steps before made: steps [{ kind: mirror, plane } | { kind: linear, direction, occurrences, spacing } | { kind: polar, axis, angle, occurrences } | { kind: scale, factor, occurrences }] — a grid is two linear steps; a bolt circle mirrored is polar then mirror. The steps stay in the body (feature_list: stepOf) and go with it; as FreeCAD's own command leaves them, the steps are hidden and listed after the MultiTransform, which is the tip and the one shown.

pd_pad.description: Pad a closed sketch into the body, along its normal: type length (length mm) | up_to_last | up_to_first | up_to_face (upToFace { at, normal } or "Face8"); sides one | two (length2 the other way) | symmetric; reversed; taper deg. The first pad takes a length. An open sketch (sketch_state first) or a pad inside the body is refused. Faces and edges are renumbered: query again. Reply: feature, volume mm³, volumeChange, faces, solids, box, health. A failure is refused with FreeCAD's error; nothing is kept.

pd_pipe.description: Sweep a closed profile sketch along a path sketch (all its edges, joined end to end); subtractive: true cuts it. The profile should sit across the path's start. Orientation, corners: feature_edit { Mode: "Frenet", Transition: "Round corner" }. Reply: feature, volume mm³, volumeChange, faces, solids, box, health. A failure is refused with FreeCAD's error; nothing is kept.

pd_pocket.description: Pocket a closed sketch out of the body: type length | through_all | up_to_first | up_to_face (upToFace); sides one | two (length2) | symmetric; reversed; taper. It cuts against the sketch's normal: one that cuts nothing is refused — reversed: true, or sketch on the face it enters. A cut that splits the body leaves 2 solids (allowed by its AllowCompound; health says so). Reply: feature, volume mm³, volumeChange, faces, solids, box, health. A failure is refused with FreeCAD's error; nothing is kept.

pd_polar_pattern.description: Repeat features around an axis: axis x|y|z (the body's; z) or a datum line (pd_datum), occurrences (the original counted), angle deg (360 spreads them evenly round; less is first to last), reversed; features: "all" repeats the whole body. Reply: feature, volume mm³, volumeChange, faces, solids, box, health. A failure is refused with FreeCAD's error; nothing is kept.

pd_primitive.description: A PartDesign primitive: kind box | cylinder | sphere | cone | ellipsoid | torus | prism | wedge, size { … } (mm), at [x, y, z] (a box's corner, a round one's base centre) and rotate { axis, angle } from the body's origin; subtractive: true cuts it out (it must overlap the body). Parametric, attached to the body's XY plane. Reply as pd_pad's.

pd_reorder.description: Move a feature or sketch in its body's history: after or before another one of the same body. Refused, with nothing moved, when something would then use what comes after it. Put after the tip, it becomes the tip. Reply: order, tip, afterTip (solid features past the tip, left out of the shape), volume.

pd_revolution.description: Revolve a closed sketch about an axis: axis V_Axis (default) | H_Axis (the sketch's) | x | y | z (the body's) | a datum line | a line's geometry id (from 0); angle deg (360); sides one | symmetric; reversed. The profile must not cross the axis. Two angles: feature_edit { Type: "TwoAngles", Angle2 }. Reply: feature, volume mm³, volumeChange, faces, solids, box, health. A failure is refused with FreeCAD's error; nothing is kept.

pd_shaft.description: A stepped shaft (the shaft wizard's geometry) as one plain Part solid, not in a PartDesign body: segments [{ length, diameter, diameterEnd (a taper) }] mm, from one end along axis x (or y, z); at, name. Reply: shaft, length, volume. part_fillet its shoulders; pd_clone brings it into a body.

pd_thickness.description: Shell the body: faces [{ at, normal }] (or shape_query's references or filters) to open (removed), thickness mm of the wall (1), inward unless outward: true; join arc|intersection. A wall thicker than an inside fillet fails: shell before filleting. Reply: feature, volume mm³, volumeChange, faces, solids, box, health. A failure is refused with FreeCAD's error; nothing is kept.

pd_tip.description: Read (no feature) or set a body's tip: the solid feature its shape stops at, and after which new features go in. A sketch or datum given: the solid feature before it. Features past the tip are kept but left out (afterTip) — set it back to the last one when done. Reply: tip, tipWas, afterTip, volume.

points_crop.description: Keep part of a cloud, filters combined: box [[min], [max]], near [x, y, z] with radius, plane { at, normal } (the side the normal points to); outside: true keeps the rest. specks { radius, least } drops points with fewer than least neighbours; thin mm keeps one point per cell. The cloud itself is cut down unless replace: false. Answers from, kept, min, max, box; refused, nothing changed, when no point is left.

points_export.description: Write a point cloud (mm, where it stands) to path: .ply (binary, 32-bit floats), .pcd, .asc / .xyz, .csv; <label>.ply in the output folder by default. Read back: answers count, readBack (should match), maxError. Changes nothing.

points_fit.description: Fit a shape through all of a cloud's points (crop to the one feature first): shape plane (centre, normal) | sphere (centre, diameter) | cylinder (base, axis, diameter, length; axis is a hint) | surface (a B-spline sheet over the points' own plane, one side only: degree 3, poles 6, smooth; 200000 points at most) | curve (a B-spline along a line of points; a loop closes itself: degree, tolerance). Answers rms and max (the points' distance from it, mm; a large max means the crop holds more than the feature); tolerance adds verdict fits | does not fit. make: true keeps the shape as an object (a surface or curve always is).

points_import.description: Read a point cloud file: path .asc / .xyz / .txt / .csv (x y z a line), .pcd, .ply, .e57 (where FreeCAD has the E57 library). every: keep every n-th point; scale: mm per file unit (1000 for metres). Positions only. The whole file is read into memory: thin a huge one with every. Answers object, points (kept), read, min, max, box.

points_info.description: A point cloud's points (count), min, max, box (mm, where it stands in the document), centre and spacing (typical gap between neighbours). Changes nothing.

points_merge.description: Join two or more point clouds into a new one: points [labels]; remove: true deletes the originals. Answers points (its label), count, box.

points_mesh.description: A mesh through a point cloud: method height (one side of a surface: a height field on the points' own plane, one vertex per cell mm, about six points a cell by default) | hull (convex) | poisson (closed; only in a FreeCAD built with PCL; depth). Answers mesh, facets, area, closed. Then meshobj_repair / part_from_mesh.

points_sample.description: A point cloud spread evenly over a body's, surface's or mesh's faces (object): count (5000; up to 2000000), noise mm (to try a fit as a scan would see it), seed, tolerance mm (faceting of curved faces, 0.01). Answers object, points, min, max, box.

points_structure.description: A structured copy of a point cloud (Points::Structured: the points in their order laid out as a grid): points, width (per row), height (rows; count / width when left out). width × height must equal the count, so it suits a cloud still in scan order. The original stays.

port_scaffold.description: Draft an Agent Link port of an installed FreeCAD add-on. folder: the add-on's folder, for example one in FreeCAD's Mod folder. The tool reads the add-on's files as text and never runs them. It finds each Gui.addCommand with its MenuText and ToolTip. It writes a hook file, draft tool data, core stubs, test stubs, the STE lint and a draft cookbook. The output goes only to ~/AgentLink/ports/<name>/, never into the add-on or into Agent Link. name: the name of the port (the add-on's name). overwrite: true writes the drafts again. Answer: port, folder, tools, unread, files. Then read guide_read { topic: "porting" }. Changes nothing in the document.

pref_get.description: Read FreeCAD's settings (the parameter tree Edit > Preferences writes): path a group ("BaseApp/Preferences/View"; BaseApp/Preferences when left out) answers values { name: { type Boolean | Integer | Unsigned | Float | String, value } } and groups (its subgroups, to walk down); name: one setting. Only settings ever changed are stored: one that is absent is at FreeCAD's default (refused as not found, with the names stored). Works headless. Changes nothing.

pref_import.description: Bring settings over from another settings file: by default the user.cfg of the release before this one (after a FreeCAD upgrade), or path. Merged in, the file's values winning; this FreeCAD's settings are copied to a backup first (reply: backup) and the guarded ones stay as they were; macros the new release lacks are copied too (macros: false not). Reply: from, groups, settings (how many values came in), backup, macros, guardedKept. Some (theme, toolbars) show after app_restart.

pref_pack.description: Preference packs (themes and their settings; FreeCAD's own, saved ones and add-ons'): with nothing, packs lists their names; apply: name sets every value the pack holds (reply: values, how many). The stylesheet and theme show after app_restart; navigation and colours at once. There is no un-apply: an add-on that keeps a settings history can take it back.

pref_reset.description: Take settings back to FreeCAD's defaults by removing the stored values: path (the group), names. Reply: reset, notSet (names not stored there: already at the default, or misspelt). Guarded settings are refused as in pref_set.

pref_set.description: Change FreeCAD's settings: path (the group), then name + value or values { name: value }. The type follows the stored setting's own; for one not stored yet give type (bool, int, uint, float, string) or it is taken from the value — a wrong type is stored beside the right one and FreeCAD ignores it, so check with pref_get. Reply: set { name: { was, now, type } }, appliesAtNextLaunch. Most apply at once; the theme, stylesheet, language and toolbars after app_restart. Refused for the person's own: Agent Link's ExtensionRepos, the switches add-ons guard, the Addon Manager's groups, the macro folder and program paths (…BinaryPath, …Executable).

queue_go.description: The person's go for heavy jobs held while they worked in the window: call it only on their word in chat, never by yourself. It lifts the hold; nothing else changes. Reply: wasHeld, running (the heavy tools running now), machine (this computer's preset: heavySlots, memoryCeilingGB, fan).

recompute.description: Recompute the document and list each object that failed, with FreeCAD's reason (errors). Only touched objects and what is built from them are redone; force: true marks everything touched and recomputes it all, also past the document's skip-recompute switch (slow on a big model). Reply: recomputed (how many objects FreeCAD ran; 0 with nothing touched or with skip-recompute on, said in note), ok, errors, stillTouched. Tools that change the model recompute by themselves: this is for after object_freeze, an import or a doubt.

report_read.description: FreeCAD's Report view in the window: its last lines (last, 40 by default), or only the warnings and errors (problems: true). New problem lines also come back on each answer as "report". FreeCAD's own known faults are counted once ("known"). When there are problems, first: the first problem line without its time. Window only.

robot_export.description: Write a trajectory as KUKA KRL (.src) with FreeCAD's exporter: path (relative: the session's folder; .src added); every waypoint is written as a LIN move with its speed, whatever its type (FreeCAD's compact form; full: true is refused where FreeCAD's full form writes nothing, as in 1.1). Positions are the waypoints as they are (no tool or base applied). Reply: path, lines, moves. Simulate it on the controller before running; running it is the person's.

robot_move.description: Move a robot (the one there is when robot is left out): axes [six degrees] (forward: tcp in the reply is where the tool point lands), tcp { at [x,y,z] mm, ypr [yaw, pitch, roll] degrees or axis + angle } (inverse kinematics from the pose it is in, within the axes' limits: reached false and off_mm when it could not get there, the axes then as they were), or home: true (the home pose set in FreeCAD, else all axes 0). An orientation left out means none (tool axes along the robot's) — usually unreachable: read tcp.ypr from the reply of an axes move and keep it. Reply: axes, tcp, reached.

robot_new.description: A six-axis robot (Robot::RobotObject): model kr16 | kr125 | kr210 | kr500 (KUKA kinematics and picture, where this FreeCAD ships the files) | puma (only a name for the built-in default below: no Puma's kinematics), or kinematics: a CSV of your own (a header line, then six lines of a, alpha, d, theta, rotDir, maxAngle, minAngle, velocity; mm and degrees). Without a file the robot is FreeCAD's built-in default, a KUKA IR 500 — the reply's model says which was used. tool { at, ypr }: the tool's point from the flange (a gripper's tip), which tcp in robot_move and robot_run then means. at, ypr are stored as its Base, but FreeCAD's kinematics do not use it: positions are always in the robot's own frame, origin at its foot. Reply: robot, axes [6 degrees], tcp { at, ypr }, model.

robot_path.description: A trajectory object: waypoints [{ at, ypr, type LIN | PTP | CIRC | WAIT (LIN by default), speed mm/s (1000), cont, name }], two or more, in the robot's frame — or edges ["Body.Edge3", …] (or an object for all its edges; one object only) to follow, deviation mm (0.5) from curved ones, useRotation for the edges' own orientation. Reply: trajectory, waypoints, length mm, seconds. robot_run checks a robot can follow it.

robot_run.description: Check a trajectory on a robot without moving it for good: samples (100; 2 … 5000) points along it by time, each solved by inverse kinematics from the one before, the tool point (robot_new tool) on the path. Reply: verdict (reaches all | misses n of N), misses [{ t, at, off_mm }] (the first 20), worst_mm, each axis's range of angles used, seconds. A miss is a point out of reach or past an axis limit, or one the solver could not follow to. The robot's axes are put back as they were.

robot_tool.description: Draw a tool shape on a robot's flange (Robot's Add tool shape): robot, tool (an object with a shape), at / axis + angle where on the shape the flange sits (ToolBase). Shown in the window only; it does not change the kinematics or the tool point (robot_new tool does).

robot_trajectory.description: Combine or adjust trajectories as new objects that follow their sources (FreeCAD's compound and dress-up): op join (trajectories [names], in order) | dress (trajectory, with any of: speed mm/s and acceleration for every waypoint, cont true | false, move [x,y,z] added to every waypoint and/or ypr [yaw, pitch, roll] turned on top of each one's orientation — the same path at another place or angle; add: UseOrientation makes ypr replace the orientations instead). Reply: trajectory, waypoints, seconds, length_mm.

scad_code.description: Run OpenSCAD code into the document: code (e.g. "difference() { cube(20, center=true); sphere(13); }") goes through the OpenSCAD program to CSG and comes in as scad_import does. Needs OpenSCAD installed (scad_status); a syntax error is refused with OpenSCAD's message. name: the label of the result when there is one top object. Reply: top, objects, made.

scad_export.description: Write objects (the one body when left out) as OpenSCAD CSG (path: .csg or .scad, .csg added; relative: the session's folder): Part primitives, booleans, extrusions and placements as OpenSCAD's own, anything else (PartDesign bodies, fillets, imports) as polyhedra of triangles — the note counts them. Reply: path, bytes, lines. The document is not changed.

scad_import.description: Read an OpenSCAD file into the document (path; relative: the session's folder): .csg needs only FreeCAD, unless it uses hull, minkowski or text (those, and any .scad, go through the OpenSCAD program: refused unavailable when it is not installed — scad_status). Primitives, booleans, transforms and extrusions come in as FreeCAD's own parametric objects (Part::Box, Cut, Fuse …; one object per CSG node, so a small file makes many), hull and minkowski as meshes turned to shapes. Reply: objects (how many), top (the results nothing else uses — the bodies to work with), made [{ object, type, solids, volume }], health.

scad_op.description: OpenSCAD's hull (the convex shape stretched round the objects, like shrink-wrap) or minkowski (the first shape swept round by the second: rounded edges all over; slow, minutes on curved shapes) of objects [names]. Hull works without OpenSCAD (computed here from the shapes' points, faceted on curves: made says which); minkowski needs OpenSCAD. The inputs are kept. name: the result's label. Reply: object, made, volume, faces, health.

scad_status.description: Whether the OpenSCAD program is on this computer (openscad: its path or null; version), and whether FreeCAD's CSG parser (ply) loads. Without OpenSCAD: .csg import (not a file's own hull, minkowski or text), CSG export and scad_op's hull work; .scad files, scad_code and minkowski do not. Changes nothing.

scad_tidy.description: OpenSCAD workbench's tree tools on objects: action color_code (all shapes when no objects: coloured by validity and kind — the reply's key; as FreeCAD's own Color Shapes it recomputes nothing and leaves no object touched that was not before) | explode (a top-level Part::Fuse / MultiFuse / Compound deleted, its inputs kept, shown and moved by its placement) | expand_placements (placements pushed down to the leaves) | tolerance { vertex, edge, face mm } (a copy with tolerances raised to at least these, never lowered; the original hidden) | remove_subtree (objects and everything under them that nothing else uses — deleted for good) | replace { parent, old, new } (parent uses new where it used old). Reply by action: coloured, exploded, expanded, made, removed, replaced.

section.description: Cut a body with a plane and read the cut: area mm², regions, and the outlines as [u, v] polylines in the plane (outer: false marks a hole; a point is origin + u·U + v·V, the reply's plane gives origin, normal, u, v). normal [x,y,z] or "+z" (default); at a point on the plane, or offset mm along the normal from the origin; tolerance the chord error (0.05 mm); maxPoints per outline (400). A plane that misses the body is refused with the body's box. Changes nothing (part_section makes the cut an object).

selection.description: Set the window's selection for cmd_run and menu_run to act on: objects [names or labels] replaces it with those whole objects (faces and edges are picked with gui_input clicks); no objects clears it; clear: false with no objects reads it instead (detail gives the picked faces and edges). A wrong name is refused and the selection left as it was. Reply: selected [labels], document. Window only.

session_state.description: What the document holds: each body's volume, area, faces, solids and size (mm) — every shown body, a Body of several solids too (multiSolid says how many and whether AllowCompound means it), a part attached to another (a screw) beside it — the step count, jobs running and where files go. In the window also next: one short line (under 400 characters) of what FreeCAD is in the middle of, most pressing first — a dialog in front and its buttons, a sketch open in edit with its DoF, an open task panel and its buttons, then likely next: up to 3 tools, likeliest first, each with a few words on why, ranked from the document's own state (a failing recompute first; then what is picked — an edge, a face; a sketch open in edit and whether it still has DoF; a drawing page in front; an assembly and its joints; how far the body is — no sketch yet, a closed sketch no feature uses, the last feature a pad or a fillet), leaving out a tool whose FreeCAD command on the active workbench's toolbars reports itself inactive; then the active workbench and the status bar's text. No tool is named while a dialog is in front (dialog_answer is the next step). A changing call's health carries the same line when it is news. leftOut [{ extension, error }] and warning are there while an installed add-on did not load in this FreeCAD (its tools are missing: the error says why; fix or update the add-on, then agentlink_update or app_restart). toolsChanged: the tool list is no longer the one last listed (groups enabled or hidden, an add-on installed, updated or removed) — the first time added, removed, updated and callable (new but unlisted) by name, after that the counts, until the list is read again. launcher: true adds the Claude extension's launcher as seen from here (the copy fetched from GitHub, whether it can load, its log's last lines). Changes nothing.

shape_query.description: Find a body's faces, edges or vertices by what they are; the refs it answers ("Face12", "Edge3", counted from 1) are what other tools take. kind face|edge|vertex; type plane, cylinder, cone, sphere, torus, bspline (faces) or line, circle, ellipse, bspline (edges); normal [x,y,z] (flat or curved faces, outward at the centre) or axis (a line's direction, a circle's or cylinder's axis, either way) within degrees (1); radius, area, length a number or [least, most]; x / y / z the centre's coordinate within tol (0.01); near [x,y,z] or { point, within } (nearest first); inside { min, max } (the centre in that box); of "Face6" that face's edges or vertices. sort area|radius|length|distance|x|y|z, -key largest first; limit (20; found counts all, more the rest). Reply items: ref, type, area / length, centroid / mid, normal, radius, axis, center. Trap: numbers change after any modelling step — query again rather than reuse old ones. Changes nothing.

sheet_cells.description: Merge spreadsheet cells (merge "A1:C1": the top-left cell stays, the others are cleared with their aliases) or split a merged one (split "A1", any of its cells). sheet_format { merge } does the same and first checks for aliases in use.

sheet_chart.description: A chart of a sheet's columns, written as SVG: kind line | bar | scatter (needs x), x (a range of labels or numbers), y [ranges of values, "B2:B20"], names, title, xlabel, ylabel, path. Reply: path, series, points.

sheet_clear.description: Clear a range, "A1:C4" (contents, alias, format; up to 20000 cells). Refused if an alias there is in use, unless force (then refused only if a user fails).

sheet_export.description: Write a sheet's computed values to a CSV / TSV file: path (default <sheet>.csv in the out folder), delimiter. No formulas, aliases or units (a quantity is its number in mm, deg, kg, s). Changes nothing in the document.

sheet_format.description: Format a range: style [bold, italic, underline] ([] clears), align [left|center|right, top|vcenter|bottom], color / background "#rrggbb" (null clears), displayUnit "mm" | "in" | "deg" … (how it shows; the value stays), width (column px), height (row px), merge true (the top-left cell stays, the rest are cleared) | false.

sheet_import.description: Read a CSV / TSV file into a sheet: path (in the out folder unless absolute), delimiter comma | tab | semicolon; sheet to fill one (replace: true if it holds cells: all of it goes), else a new sheet named after the file. Fields are taken as if typed ("=…" a formula).

sheet_list.description: The spreadsheets (the Params sheet too): cells used, their range, aliases and what uses them, design tables. Changes nothing.

sheet_new.description: Make an empty spreadsheet: name (its label). The reply's name is what expressions use: <name>.A1, <name>.<alias>, or <<label>>.<alias>.

sheet_read.description: Read a sheet's cells: content ("=A1 * 2"; text has a leading '), computed value and unit, alias, or error (FreeCAD's reason); empty: true for an empty cell. range "A1:D20" or cells [..] narrows (400 cells a call); format: true adds style, alignment, colours, display unit. Shows bound ranges and design tables. Changes nothing.

sheet_rows.description: Insert or remove rows or columns: action insert | remove, rows (the first row's number, from 1; new rows go above it) or columns (the first column's letters), count. References and aliases move with the cells; removing a cell in use is refused.

sheet_set.description: Write cells as if typed in FreeCAD, then recompute: cells { A1: 12, B1: "=A1 * 2", C1: "10 mm", D1: "text", E1: null (clears) }, or rows [[…], …] from at (default A1); text: true keeps strings as text. aliases { B2: "width" } ("" removes) names a cell for expressions (<Sheet>.width): a letter, then letters, digits, _; not a cell address, a unit (m, mm, s, N, A …) or e, pi. A formula FreeCAD cannot parse, a failing cell or a feature it breaks is refused, nothing kept. Reply: cells; drives and bodies when an alias is in use.

sheet_table.description: Design tables (configurations), FreeCAD's own kind: action make { params [names; alias rules as sheet_set], configs [{ name, values [..] | { param: value } }], units { param: "mm" | "deg" | "" } (numbers default mm), sheet (else a new one), at (the header cell; the active row is under it), owner (the object carrying the switch; default the one Body, else a group holding the sheet), property (default Configuration), active } — then bind properties to <Sheet>.<param> with param_bind; use { config } switches and answers the bodies; add { config, values } adds a row; list. guide_read sheet.

show.description: Show or hide objects in the window as the tree's eye does: objects (names or labels; left out or "all": every body and top-level shape), visible (true; false hides). A PartDesign body shown also shows its tip, the finished part. Reply: visible or hidden [labels], unknown (names not found; the rest still done). Hidden parts are left out of view_render and of checks that go by what is shown. Window only.

sketch_add.description: Add geometry to a sketch, in its own x/y (mm; angles deg, counter-clockwise from +x): items [{ kind, …, construction, dims, name }]. kinds: line {from, to}; polyline {points, closed}; arc {center, radius, start, end} (always ccw from start to end); arc3 {points: start, through, end}; circle {center, radius|diameter}; circle3 {points: three on it}; ellipse {center, major, minor (full sizes), rotation}; parabola {vertex, focal, rotation, from, to}; hyperbola {center, major, minor (semi-axes), rotation, from, to}; bspline {points it passes through, closed — or interpolate: false, points its poles, degree}; rectangle {center|corner, size [w,h]}; rounded_rectangle {…, radius}; polygon {center, radius (to corners), sides, rotation}; slot {from, to (end centres), radius}; arc_slot {center, radius (its middle), width, start, end}; point {at}.
