A shape comes with its own coincident/horizontal/vertical/tangent/equal constraints; separate items are not joined to each other (sketch_constrain coincident or tangent does that). dims: true adds its sizes as constraints (named <name>_width, _height, _d, _r, _length when named — what param_bind binds). Answers added [{ ids: geometry ids from 0 in the order made (a polygon's last is its construction circle), constraints: [first, last] ids, dims }] and state (dof, closedWires, openVertices, readyForFeature). Vertices: 1 start, 2 end, 3 centre.

sketch_array.description: An array of geometry in a sketch: rows (along y), cols (along x) and spacing [dx, dy] mm, the original counted (constrain: true keeps the spacing as constraints; clone: true keeps copies equal), or polar { center, count, angle (default 360) }. Answers new: the ids added.

sketch_attach.description: Move a sketch onto another plane (Sketcher's map/reorient): plane XY | XZ | YZ | a datum plane | "Pad.Face3", or face { at, normal, feature? }; offset mm along its normal, rotate deg in it, flip. A face is bound to the feature that made it (the earliest in the body that has it, or feature), not the tip; a sketch that sits before that feature is moved after it (refused when a feature is built from it).

sketch_bspline.description: Edit a B-spline in a sketch: geo, op degree (by: +1 raises, -1 lowers) | knot (param: insert a knot there, multiplicity; or knot: its index from 1 and by: raise/lower its multiplicity — a corner at 0 continuity). Answers degree, poles, knots, multiplicities.

sketch_carbon.description: Copy another sketch's geometry and constraints into this one (Sketcher's carbon copy): from, construction: true brings it as construction. Its dimensions stay bound to the source's by expression. Answers new: the ids added.

sketch_constrain.description: Constrain a sketch: constraints [{ type, refs, value, name }]. A ref is FreeCAD's: a geometry id g, a point p = [g, vertex] (1 start, 2 end, 3 centre) or "origin"; -1 the horizontal axis, -2 the vertical, -3 down outside edges. types and their refs: coincident [p, p]; point_on_object [p, g]; horizontal | vertical [g] or [p, p]; parallel | perpendicular | equal [g, g]; tangent [g, g] or end points [p, p]; symmetric [p, p, g] (about a line) or [p, p, p]; distance [g] (length), [p, p] or [p, g]; distance_x | distance_y [g], [p] (from the origin) or [p, p] (second minus first); radius | diameter [g], all mm; angle [g] (from +x) or [g, g] (first to second, ccw), deg; fix [p] (a point held where it is) or [g] (blocked: add it last). name it to bind it to a parameter later. All or nothing: one that conflicts or is redundant is refused, naming what clashes, and nothing added. Answers added (constraint ids from 0) and state.

sketch_copy.description: Copy geometry in a sketch (move: true moves it instead): geometry [ids] (default every non-construction one), and by [dx, dy] (clone: true keeps copies equal to the originals), rotate { center, angle deg ccw } or scale { center, factor }. by copies the constraints among them too; rotate and scale give plain geometry. Answers new: the copies' ids.

sketch_edit.description: Edit a sketch; several keys may go in one call, done in this order: move { geo, vertex (0 the whole curve, 1/2/3), to [x,y] } (drags it as far as its constraints let it), set [{ constraint: id|name, value mm|deg }], construction { geo, on }, rename { constraint, name }, deleteConstraints [id|name], delete [geometry ids — their constraints go too], fillet { at: [g, v] a corner, or geos [g1, g2] near [[x,y],[x,y]]; radius; chamfer: true cuts it straight } (the curves trimmed to it), trim { geo, at [x,y] } (cuts off the piece there, between crossings), split { geo, at }, mirror { geos, about: "x" | "y" | "origin" | a line id } (free mirrored copies: no symmetric constraints are added), group [geos] (held as one, FreeCAD 1.2), text { text, at, height, font, construction } (letters as geometry), exposeInternal [geos] (an ellipse's axes or a B-spline's poles back as construction geometry), removeAxesAlignment [geos]. delete, fillet, trim and split renumber geometry: read sketch_state before using ids again. Answers done, state, geometryCount, and bodyAfter when features are built on it; an edit that breaks one is refused with FreeCAD's error and nothing kept.

sketch_extend.description: Lengthen (or shorten) a line or arc of a circle at one end: geo, end 1 | 2 (default 2), by mm (negative shortens; along the arc for an arc), or to: another curve's id a line should reach.

sketch_external.description: Bring edges of the body's solid (its tip) into a sketch as outside geometry to constrain to: edges ["Edge7" or a query { type: circle|line, radius, axis, near, inside } as shape_query takes — safer: edge numbers change with edits]. Answers ids (negative, -3 down, in order) for sketch_constrain's refs; a constraint to them follows the part. Refused when the tip is built from this sketch. From a datum, binder or other sketch: sketch_project.

sketch_join.description: Join two open curves' ends into one B-spline: a [geo, vertex], b [geo, vertex] (vertex 1 | 2, different curves), continuity 0 (corner) or 1 (smooth). It replaces both: ids change; answers bspline, its id.

sketch_merge.description: Merge sketches into a new one on the first's plane, geometry and constraints kept (not those to outside geometry): sketches [names]; remove: true deletes the originals. Answers sketch: its label.

sketch_mirror.description: A mirrored copy of a whole sketch as a new sketch on the same plane: about y (left-right) | x (up-down) | origin. Geometry only, no constraints. Answers sketch: its label.

sketch_new.description: A new sketch in a body, on plane XY | XZ | YZ | a datum plane's name | "Pad.Face3", or on a face of the solid found by face { at: a point on it, normal: its outward normal } — never by face index, which changes after edits. One of plane or face. offset mm along the normal; flip reverses it. A face sketch is lined up with the world: its x along the world axis that lies most in the face. Answers sketch (its label) and frame: where sketch x/y and its origin lie in the world.

sketch_offset.description: Offset a sketch's profile by distance mm (out; negative in): its geometry ids (all but construction when left out), joined end to end; join arc (round corners, the default), tangent or intersection (sharp). Answers added: the new geometry's ids. The offset is plain geometry with no constraints: it does not follow later edits unless constrained (sketch_constrain; sketch_validate fix joins its pieces).

sketch_project.description: Bring edges of a binder, datum or another sketch of the same body into this sketch as external geometry: from, edges ["Edge3" | { near, kind }] (default all), defining: true makes them part of the profile (FreeCAD 1.1 on). Answers ids (-3 down, in order) for sketch_constrain. The body's own solid: sketch_external.

sketch_state.description: The solver's reading of a sketch — check it before a feature: dof (0 is fully constrained), conflicting / redundant / malformed constraint ids, closed wires and open vertices, readyForFeature with todo when not; its frame in the world; detail (default true) lists geometry and constraints with ids, values (mm; deg for angles) and refs [g, vertex]. Ids count from 0 in every sketch tool. A pad on a sketch with dof > 0 works but moves when edited.

sketch_to_bspline.description: Convert geometry to B-splines in place (to reshape by poles, or join): geometry [ids]. Geometry ids stay; its constraints other than end-point coincidences are removed.

sketch_validate.description: Check a sketch the way Sketcher's Validate does: degenerate geometry, ends that touch with no coincidence, invalid, redundant and conflicting constraints (precision mm); answers found. fix: true repairs what it can (not conflicts; a failed repair leaves the sketch as it was); autoconstrain: true also adds the obvious coincident/horizontal/vertical constraints.

snapshot_latest.description: The person's newest screenshot (index 2, 3 … for older ones) as a picture with their marks (original: true without), with its note, numbered pins and their comments, workbench and time; a note says when they are still marking it up. Only the person takes them (the camera button, Alt+Shift+S): none yet is refused. Changes nothing.

snapshot_list.description: The person's screenshots, newest first, without the pictures: time, note, pins, saved path. snapshot_latest { index } shows one. Changes nothing.

steps_list.description: A PartDesign body's history in order (body may be left out when there is one): each feature's step number, name, label, type, its key value, the volume after it and what it added or took away (sketches: true lists the sketches too). The same list Agent Link's Steps tab plays. Changes nothing.

steps_render.description: The build played back as pictures, drawn headless (not the window): a PNG a feature (step_01.png …), framed on the finished part so it grows in place, each captioned with its step, type and what it did, and a contact sheet steps.png of them all (sheet: false leaves it out; inline: false keeps it out of the reply). body; view (iso, or top, front, right …); width, height pixels a picture (480 × 360); path a folder (steps_<body> in the session's folder). Tessellates every step: seconds a step on a heavy body. Reply: folder, files, sheet, steps. The model is not changed.

surface_blend.description: A blend curve joining two edges smoothly (Surface BlendCurve, parametric): start / end { edge "Body.Edge3", at 0…1 along it (default: start 0, end 1), continuity 0…4 (1 tangent, 2 curvature, default), size (1; the tangent there is size × the distance between the two points, so 5 swings wide; negative leaves against the edge's direction) }. Reply: object, edges 1, length. Use it as a boundary for the next surface.

surface_boundary.description: A surface bounded by 2–4 curves meeting end to end, given going round (Surface GeomFillSurface, parametric): edges, fill stretched (default, flattest) | coons | curved (rounder). Lines and arcs are taken as B-splines. When coons or curved is refused for curves that do not match, a Surface Filling through the same edges is made instead (reply: note). Reply: object, fill, sides, area.

surface_cut.description: Cut a surface by another object (Surface Cut, a boolean cut that follows both): surface, by. By a solid: what lies inside it is removed. By a surface: nothing is removed, the surface comes back split along where they cross (reply: note; part_extract takes a piece). Reply: object, of, by, faces, area.

surface_extend.description: Run a face on past its edges (Surface Extend, parametric): face "Body.Face2"; u and v, how far past each pair of opposite edges as a share of its size that way (0.05 = 5% at each end; -0.5 … 10). The result is a new four-sided B-spline surface within 0.1 mm of the face; holes and a trimmed outline are not kept. Reply: object, area.

surface_fill.description: A plain surface filled across one closed boundary (Part's filled face; not parametric): edges ("Body.Edge3" …) or a sketch or wire whose outline bounds it, bent as smoothly as the edges allow; thickness mm makes it a solid (negative: the other side). Edges that leave a gap or form more than one loop are refused. Reply: object, area, solid, volume.

surface_loft.description: A plain surface through curves in order (Part's loft; not parametric): curves, each an edge ("Body.Edge3"), a sketch, or { points: [[x,y,z] …], closed } for a smooth curve through them; all open (a sheet) or all closed (a tube), running the same way. ruled: straight between; closed: true joins the last back to the first (3 or more); thickness mm makes it a solid (side out, in or both). Reply: object, area, solid, volume, size, through; warnings under 0.8 mm or when the solid is not valid.

surface_points.description: A plain smooth surface through a grid of points, row by row (rows: [[[x,y,z] …] …], two or more rows of one length): through every point, or with tolerance mm within that of them for a smoother one. thickness and side make it a solid. Reply: grid, fitted, farthestPoint mm (how far the worst point is off it), area.

surface_polynomial.description: A polynomial (quadric) surface fitted by least squares to a mesh's or point cloud's points, as a 3 × 3 Bézier patch over their extent (as Reverse Engineering's Polynomial Surface): from, name. For a patch that is one smooth bowl or saddle; split a scan with meshobj_segments or meshobj_trim first. Reply: surface, points, rms and max mm off the points (along the fit plane's normal).

surface_sections.description: A surface through curves in order (Surface Sections, parametric: it follows them): sections ["Body.Edge3" | a wire or sketch's name …], two or more, each one open curve, all running the same way; every edge of a named wire is a section of its own. Reply: object, sections, faces, area, closed.

surface_sew.description: Sew surfaces into one shell (Surface Sewing, parametric): faces [surface objects (all their faces), or "Body.Face3"], two or more whose edges meet within tolerance mm (0.01). solid: true also makes a closed shell a solid body (a plain copy). Reply: faces, shells, closed, area; solid { body, volume }, or why not (the shell is open); warning when nothing joined.

surface_thicken.description: Make a surface a solid: surface an object ("Surface") or one face ("Body.Face3"), thickness mm over 0, side out (along its normal), in, or both (half each way). A new plain object; it cannot be thicker inward than its tightest bend. Reply: object, solid, volume, area, size; warnings under two printed lines (0.8 mm) or when the solid is not valid.

td_area.description: Write a face's area on the drawing with a leader to it: face ("Body.Face3" on the part), view, unit mm2 | cm2 | m2, decimals, format ("A = {value} {unit}"), at. Written as text: it does not follow the part afterwards.

td_balloon.description: A balloon pointing at a feature of a view: view, on (a ref as td_dim takes), text (default the page's next number), at [dx, dy] paper mm from the view's centre. Its tip and bubble are kept as FreeCAD keeps them, in the view's own unscaled frame (OriginX/Y, X/Y over the view's scale).

td_bim.description: A BIM section plane drawn on a page (a building plan or section): section (from bim_section), scale (0.02 = 1:50), at, render Wireframe | Solid, fill (cut faces hatched), spaces, hidden. Warns when it drew nothing.

td_centermarks.description: Centre marks (thin chain crosses) on the holes and round edges of views (all part views when left out): extend mm past each circle (2); on: false takes them off. Whole circles and arcs past a half turn only. Drawn by td_export; in the window the same chain lines are drawn as FreeCAD's own cosmetic centre lines on those circles only, and FreeCAD's own crosses of the view (its ArcCenterMarks, which mark every arc's centre, a slot's ends too) are switched off.

td_cosmetic.description: Cosmetic geometry on a view (FreeCAD's own cosmetic edges from 1.1, so in the window too; always in td_export): items [{ kind line (from, to: points on the part) | circle (center on the part, radius mm) | centerline (edges: a shaft's or hole's two side lines; extend mm) | thread (edges: the two outline lines of a side view, or circle: the end view's round edge; internal: true for a tapped hole; pitch, ISO coarse by default; length mm) , style thin | visible | hidden | center }]; clear: true drops the earlier ones. td_lines takes them by order, from 0.

td_datum.description: A datum feature symbol: view, letter, on the feature ("Edge3" or { edge: { through } }, { point }), at. The triangle stands on the feature, the letter outward.

td_detail.description: A detail view: a circle of radius (mm on the part) around center [x, y, z] (a point on the part) or anchor [x, y] (td_geometry's view mm), drawn larger (scale, default twice the base), symbol (B …), at. 0 edges in the answer: the circle misses the part.

td_dim.description: A dimension on a view, measured by TechDraw so it follows the part: type distance | horizontal | vertical (two points or one straight edge) | radius | diameter (one round edge) | angle (two straight edges); refs ["Vertex1", "Vertex4"] or by the part, which holds when numbers move: { point: [x,y,z] }, { circle: { diameter, near } }, { center: { diameter, near } }, { edge: { through: [p, q] } }. A diameter by { circle } takes whole circles only: an arc of that size (a slot's end) is refused — use radius. at [dx, dy] (its text from the view's centre, page mm); tolerance at once: plus/minus, fit "H7", basic, label, format "%.1f". Lengths in an iso view read foreshortened (td_dim_special axo_length). Answers dimension (its name), measured, text; unmeasurable is refused, nothing kept.

td_dim_align.description: Line dimensions' texts up: dims (the first sets the line), direction horizontal (all at the first's height) | vertical | oblique (three or more, on the line through the first two).

td_dim_format.description: Dimension text: dims, then decimals n (0 to 9), more +1/−1, prefix diameter (⌀) | square (□) | count (n×, with count) | any text, removePrefix, format (a whole format, "%.2f mm"). A prefix is text only: it does not check what the dimension is on.

td_dim_repair.description: Point a dimension at new references (after the model changed and its numbers moved): refs as td_dim takes them, view to move it to another; the old ones are put back if TechDraw cannot measure the new.

td_dim_special.description: Special dimensions: kind extent_h / extent_v (the view's whole width or height, or refs edges'), chamfer_h / chamfer_v (refs a chamfer's two points: "2 x45°"), arc_length (refs one arc: ◠ its length), axo_length (refs [edge, extension-line edge] in an iso view: the true length, not the foreshortened one). at [dx, dy]. Arc and axo lengths are text, re-read from the part when a td_ tool changes the drawing.

td_dimset.description: Several dimensions along one direction at once: style chain (each point to the next) or baseline (each from the first, stacked lanes); type horizontal | vertical; refs three or more points in order (as td_dim takes them); offset mm off the view (10), spacing between lanes (7), format. Answers each dimension and overall.

td_export.description: Write a page out: formats [svg, pdf, dxf], name. DXF is TechDraw's own. SVG and PDF are drawn here from the page's objects (TechDraw's own PDF and SVG export needs the window): views, dimensions, symbols, notes, tables, centre marks, hatching and the title block's fields, without the template's artwork. Files go to the session's folder; notes says what was skipped; stacked names dimensions whose texts lie on one spot (td_dim_align or object_set X, Y moves one).

td_finish.description: A surface texture symbol (ISO 1302) on a surface's edge in a view (on): ra ("1.6" or "Rz 6.3"), removal required (machined) | prohibited | any, process ("ground"), lay = | perpendicular | crossed | multi | circular | radial | particulate, allowance mm; placed off the part on a leader (at [x, y] page mm to choose where; onSurface: true stands it on the edge itself).

td_gdt.description: A feature control frame (ISO 1101 / ASME Y14.5): frame [{ characteristic (flatness, straightness, circularity, cylindricity, profile_line, profile_surface, parallelism, perpendicularity, angularity, position, concentricity, symmetry, circular_runout, total_runout), tolerance mm, diameter (⌀ zone), modifier M|L|…, datums ["A", "B|M"] }] (rows stack: composite); with a leader to on (a view ref) or under dimension; at. Form tolerances take no datum, orientation and runout need one (refused, saying which). Answers reads: the frame in words.

td_geometry.description: A view's geometry, to dimension against: kind edges | circles (each marked circle or arc) | lines | vertices, each with its ref (Edge3, Vertex5: zero-based), kind, ends or centre and diameter (mm on the part); limit (120). The numbers move when the part changes: read them just before use, or name geometry by the part (byPoint). Changes nothing.

td_hatch.description: Hatch faces of the part in a view (thin lines spacing mm apart at angle degrees; a section's cut is hatched by itself): view, faces ["Face6" …] (the part's own, from shape_query) — none takes it off. Drawn by td_export, and in the window as FreeCAD's own hatch (TechDraw::DrawHatch, its default pattern) on the view's face that shows each (window says which, or why none); a face seen edge-on is warned of.

td_leader.description: A leader line from a feature of a view (on: a ref as td_dim takes) to at [x, y] page mm, with text (\n splits lines) at its end — a note pointing at something.

td_lines.description: A view's lines: action align_h / align_v { refs two points or an edge } (the view turned so they line up) | style { refs edges, style solid|dashed|dotted|dashdot|dashdotdot|none, weight mm, color } | extend / shorten { items (td_cosmetic's lines by order from 0; all when left out), by mm, centerlines } | erase { items, tags } (cosmetic lines gone; all td_cosmetic's when items is left out).

td_list.description: A page's views (label, scale, size, edge count; a group's items), dimensions (name, refs, measured, text, tolerance), GD&T, other objects and title block. A document just opened holds each view's settings but not its lines (FreeCAD works them out at the view's first recompute): views without lines are computed here first and waited for (up to 20 s; computed says how many and how long), and the dimensions on them after. A view still without lines is marked notReady with no edge count, and a dimension on it has notReady in place of measured and text — never 0 as if measured; notReady at the top says which and what to do (recompute, then td_list again). Changes nothing in the model.

td_note.description: A note on the page: text (\n splits lines), size (mm, 5), at [x, y] page mm. td_leader points one at a feature.

td_page.description: TechDraw pages: action new { paper A4|A3|A2|A1|A0|Letter|ANSIB…, orientation landscape|portrait, standard iso|asme, blank, template (an SVG path, or a name from templates), projection first|third, scale (the page's: views take it unless given their own), name } on the build's own templates, sample title-block texts cleared; list; read { page } (views and title-block fields); templates. Page positions are mm from the paper's bottom-left corner, y up.

td_projection.description: A projection group (views kept aligned): views [front, top, right, left, rear, bottom, iso, isoLeft …] (front always; default front, top, right), projection first|third (default the page's), front (which way is front: a direction), bodies, scale, at. Answers items: each one's label (Front, Top, FrontTopRight …) is the view td_dim and td_section take.

td_section.description: A section view cut from a view: normal of the cut plane, toward who looks at the section ("x" | "-y" | [x,y,z]; it lies across the base view, not along its direction), through [x, y, z] a point of the plane (default the part's middle), symbol (A …), at, hatch false. Answers its label (Section A) and edges; 0 edges: the plane misses the part.

td_section_position.description: Line a section view up with its base view: straight across when it sits beside it, straight above or below when over it.

td_table.description: A spreadsheet's cells as a table on the page (a parts list from asm_bom, a revision table): sheet, range (default its used cells), size, at. It follows the sheet; an empty sheet is refused. size: the text's height on the paper, mm (3.5): the table's scale is set for it (reply: scale).

td_title.description: The title block: fields { name: value } by the template's own field names, which differ by template (no fields: lists them; an unknown name is refused with the list); preset "mine" fills from a saved one, with save: true saves the page's as it (not its title, sheet number, scale or date, unless given in fields), delete: true removes it; import / export a presets file (JSON). Ask the person for names and numbers.

td_tolerance.description: Tolerance a dimension (by its name or label): plus/minus (mm; equal = ±), fit "H7" | "g6" (ISO 286 deviations for its measured size), basic: true (a boxed theoretically exact size, for GD&T), label (text instead of the value), format "%.2f"; clear: true first resets it.

td_view.description: Put a view of bodies on a page: bodies (all when left out), direction front|top|right|left|rear|bottom|iso or [x, y, z] (part toward viewer), scale (left out: the page's), at [x, y] page mm (its centre, bottom-left origin), hidden (dashed hidden lines), name. Answers its label (what other td_ tools take), size on the paper and edges — 0 edges: the bodies are empty or hidden. Its lines are waited for (up to 30 s in the window).

td_view_more.description: More views on a page: kind broken { view, breaks, gap } | draft { object (a Draft object) } | clip { width, height, frame } | clip_add / clip_remove { clip, view } | image { path, width, height } | symbol { path (an SVG), scale } | share { view } (the view also on this page, with its dimensions) | lock { view, locked } | stack { view, to top|bottom|up|down } | move { view, page } (to another page; a group's item takes its group), at [x, y].

td_weld.description: A weld symbol on a leader from a feature of a view (on, as td_dim takes it; at the leader's end on the page), drawn by td_export, and in the window as FreeCAD's own weld symbol on the leader (TechDraw::DrawWeldSymbol, with FreeCAD's own symbol for fillet, square, v, plug and surfacing; the other kinds show their words only, and window says which): kind fillet, square, v, bevel, u, j, plug, spot, seam, flare-v, flare-bevel, backing, surfacing, size (left of it), length (right: "50" or "50-100" for pitch), side arrow | other | both, allAround, field (a site weld), tail (process, "GMAW").

text_document.description: A text document kept in the file (App::TextDocument), for notes that travel with the model: name (found by label, made if new; "Notes" by default), text replaces what it holds, append: true adds a line instead; with no text it only reads the size. Reply: text (its label), chars, lines. It shows in the tree; the person reads it by double-clicking.

tool_find.description: Find a tool by plain words (what it does, FreeCAD's own command or workbench name): up to limit (8) tools, best first, each with its group, one line of what it does and listed (whether the client was shown it). queries: up to 6 searches in one call. tool: a name or a list of names answers each one's whole description and inputs (its card); groups: true the tool groups and what each holds; group narrows a search. Every tool is callable by name, listed or not (where the client sends only listed tools: batch { calls: [{ tool, arguments }] }). listing: true answers what the client is shown now (mode, style, count, tokens, names); to: a .json file gets the whole listing. Changes nothing.

tool_groups.description: The tool groups, which are listed and what each holds (count, about); enable / disable: [group …] lists or hides them (core stays); group: g answers with that group alone (its whole about and its tools, each with one line of what it does); detail: true gives every group's whole about. The cheap way to a tool that is not listed is find, card, call: find: "words" searches every tool (best first; group narrows it, limit 1-40, 10 by default) by its name, FreeCAD's own names for its commands and workbench ("PartDesign_Fillet", "techdraw", "drawing"), search words and description — tools matching every word come before those matching some — and answers name, group and what it does; tool: name (or up to 20 names) answers that tool's whole description and inputSchema (and said: words its answers gave once and now leave out, named in saidBefore); then call it by name. now: true (alone or with find) answers the tools that fit the present state, best first, each with fits (why): first the likely next step by the document's own state, the same ranking as session_state's next (next [{ tool, why }], at most three; fits then starts "likely next: …"), then the active workbench, a sketch open in edit, the selection, and whether the tool's FreeCAD command reports itself active — without a window it goes by the document's objects only and says so. With no arguments the answer also names installed add-ons that brought no tools (addonsWithoutTools [{ extension, error }] and warning), when there are any. None of these lists anything, so a group's other descriptions are not loaded: enable a group only when a task uses most of it. Every tool is callable by name either way. Changes nothing but which tools are listed. needs: tool reads that tool's own leading checks against the document now, never run — { applies: true | false | null (not checked), wouldRefuse [{ code, words }], notChecked }; arguments: {…} reads that call's checks too; advice only. find's hits that would refuse now come last, with applies: false; now: true carries appliesNow, the full form of the health's appliesNow line.

units_convert.description: A quantity in other units (FreeCAD's units calculator): value a number with its unit ("2.5 in", "300 N*m", "45 deg"), to a unit of the same kind ("mm", "lbf*ft", "rad"; * / ^ join units). Different kinds are refused. Reply: result (a number), text. Changes nothing.

usage_report.description: What working through Agent Link has cost the agent, estimated on this side: calls, tokens (text at ~3.5 characters a token, pictures by size) and the tool list each session loads up front — per day over days (7), per session, the costliest tools, and tips to cut it. session: true gives this session alone. Not Claude's own count: the plan's usage page has that. Changes nothing. appliesNow: this session's meter of the applies-now filter (notThenAnswered must stay near zero).

varset_new.description: Make a variable set (App::VarSet, FreeCAD 1.0 on): name (its label), properties { size: "55 mm" (a length), angle: "30 deg", count: 3, ratio: 0.5, on: true, note: "text" } as its variables (names: letters, digits, _; not a unit or constant), group (Variables). Expressions read them as <object name>.size (the reply's refAs) — param_bind { target, expression: "Dims.size" } takes the label too.

varset_set.description: Set or add variables of a variable set: varset (its label; may be left out when there is one), properties { name: value } as varset_new takes them (an existing one keeps its kind: a length takes "60 mm", not text). Everything bound to them recomputes; a value that breaks a feature is refused and nothing kept. Reply: variables, usedBy, bodies.

view_maps.description: The maps and layers view_render can draw here (add-ons add theirs), and the views.

view_render.description: Draw the parts as a picture and look at it — works headless. The parts shown, without the containers that hold them (an assembly, an App::Part, a group); hidden parts are not drawn and the answer names them (hidden); objects: [names] draws those named. views: one or several ("all": iso, top, front, right, each fitted). map: wall (thickness, red thin), stress (the last fea_solve), heat (the last fea_heat), or an add-on's (view_maps lists them) — with a legend and the worst spot's at; range [lo, hi] fixes the colours. section { axis x|y|z, offset mm, flip } cuts it open (cut faces hatched). zoom { at, size mm } frames a spot — a finding's at. layers: which add-on layers (a scan …). The PNG comes back as an image (inline false: the file only) and is written to path. Limits: sized before it draws (every layer's triangles times the views, timed from past renders here: time gives took and expected). Past about 40 s the big layers are drawn thinned (thinned: from and to; a map's min, max and worst are still read on every point) and a larger detail is capped (detailCapped). At 90 s into the call (a batch's start, in a batch) it stops drawing and names the views left (cut): fewer views, a zoom or a smaller picture draws them. An empty picture is answered in words, with no image sent: empty says why and what to do — no shown body (the document is empty, every part is hidden, or nothing has a solid shape), the objects named have no solid shape (notDrawn names them when others were drawn), the zoom or section leaves the parts out of frame or under 0.2% of the picture (with the parts' box), or the map has no data (no solve in this session, no wall read). fitted: false marks a picture framed by zoom rather than fitted to the parts. Shown meshes are drawn too (an imported STL, a texture result), not with a map. The map's own reading has until 40 s into the call: a blend that would take longer is thinned before it starts (detailCapped says so); time.map gives its seconds, and expected includes them.

view_snapshot.description: Save the FreeCAD window's own 3D view as the person sees it (view: turn it to a standard view first, fit true) and look at it. views [..] (up to 6, or "all") gives one grid picture of them, each view's file in paths, and puts the person's view back. width and height (800 x 600) are the whole picture — the grid with several views, split among them; cell: true makes them each view's size instead. The answer gives the sizes as saved. When nothing with a shape is shown (an empty document, everything hidden), or the model lies outside the frame or is under 6 pixels across as the view stands, the answer is empty with the reason and what to do, and no picture is taken. fitted: false with fitNote says the view was not re-fitted (no view given: as the person left it; or fit: false), so parts may be cut off. Needs the window; view_render draws without one.

window_snapshot.description: A picture of the FreeCAD window as the person sees it (toolbars, tree, panels, 3D view), or part: one dock panel by its title ("Report view", "Model", "Agent Link"; a wrong title lists them). Drawn by Qt in the background: no screen recording, the window need not be in front. path: a .png (window.png in the session's folder); inline: false leaves the picture out of the reply. Reply: path, width, height. For how something looks, never as proof a step worked: read state for that. Window only.

workbench.description: The window's workbenches: with nothing, active (its internal name, e.g. PartDesignWorkbench) and workbenches (their menu names); activate: a menu name or internal name ("Part Design", "BIM", "FEM") switches to it, loading it the first time (seconds; its commands and menus exist only from then on). Reply: active, was. Changing tools switch workbench by themselves; this is for cmd_run and menu_run. Window only.
